item_title: Ticker Report reported TeraWulf's chief financial officer said Google's credit support for Anthropic's lease at the Justified campus covers an Anthropic default after the lease starts (Nov 9)
mechanism: A hyperscaler backstop moves the tenant's default risk to Google, so the host can borrow against the lease at a rate that reflects Google's credit, not Anthropic's.

scenarios.direction: Anthropic reaches investment-grade ratings and the support falls away as described.
scenarios.why: The CFO's description, as relayed, says the support ends if Anthropic reaches specified ratings, after which the project debt rests on Anthropic's own credit.

scenarios.direction: Hyperscaler backstops become the standard way miners and neoclouds finance leases to AI labs.
scenarios.why: Lenders price the lease on the backstop's credit, which lowers the host's cost of debt for each further lab lease.
scenarios.precedent: Google backstopped Fluidstack's lease obligations at TeraWulf's Lake Mariner site in 2025 and Fluidstack's lease at Cipher Mining later that year.

scenarios.direction: Google's contingent exposure to Anthropic grows with each lease it supports.
scenarios.why: Each backstop adds a possible assumption or termination payment tied to Anthropic's performance, partly offset by the recovery from the tenant.

context_note: The standing capital-context snapshot, last refreshed 2026-08-25, has readings on rates, credit, flows and conflict but none on lease financing or hyperscaler credit support.

item_title: TechCrunch reported, citing the Financial Times, that Anthropic is spending $3.4 billion on Caterpillar natural gas generators capable of producing up to 1.7 gigawatts that equipment supplier OnePWR had originally ordered (Nov 9)
mechanism: Buying generators outright moves Anthropic from renting compute toward owning power assets, trading lease flexibility for delivery certainty and fuel-price exposure.

scenarios.direction: Other AI labs buy generators directly instead of relying on developers to secure them.
scenarios.why: With turbine backlogs reported into the early 2030s, equipment already in a queue is scarce, so a lab with cash gains by taking the order itself.
scenarios.precedent: Crusoe ordered 29 GE Vernova LM2500XPRESS turbines, about 1 GW, for AI data centers, booked in December 2024 and June 2025.

scenarios.direction: Natural gas prices rise and the cost case for on-site generation weakens.
scenarios.why: TechCrunch cited an analyst who expects prices could more than triple by the end of the decade in some markets, and the fuel bill falls on whoever runs the units.

scenarios.direction: Air-permit and local opposition limits where the generators can be run.
scenarios.why: On-site gas has drawn enforcement fights, and MIT Technology Review reported voters approving 40 of 41 anti-data-center ballot measures.
scenarios.precedent: A federal judge denied xAI's motion to dismiss an NAACP suit over permits for the gas turbines powering Colossus near Memphis, per TechCrunch.

context_note: The standing capital-context snapshot, last refreshed 2026-08-25, has readings on rates, credit, flows and conflict but none on power equipment or gas prices.

item_title: Markets Daily reported Akamai expects fourth-quarter capital expenditures of $2.445 billion to $2.645 billion, including approximately $1.7 billion to pre-purchase memory and other critical components for its Anthropic contract (Nov 8)
mechanism: Buying memory ahead of an AI lab's contract puts component inflation on Akamai's balance sheet, with a price clause passing part of any later rise back to the customer.

scenarios.direction: Component prices keep climbing and the contract's pricing adjustment passes later increases on to Anthropic.
scenarios.why: Akamai has secured about 70% of the hardware and memory, and the relayed clause covers components not yet ordered, so the rest carries the repricing.
scenarios.precedent: The Verge reported on Nov 3 that Apple warned rising memory costs would squeeze its holiday-quarter margins.

scenarios.direction: Anthropic exercises its $9 billion option and Akamai takes on a second, larger pre-purchase cycle.
scenarios.why: The 2028 outlook assumes no further orders under the option, so any exercise would add capital spending beyond the guided range.

scenarios.direction: Akamai raises outside financing to fund the build and its 2027 convertible maturity.
scenarios.why: Its plan relies on about $4.2 billion of cash and on operating cash flow, potentially supplemented by financing, while it aims to keep an investment-grade rating.

context_note: The standing capital-context snapshot, last refreshed 2026-08-25, has credit and rate readings but none on memory prices or component pre-purchases.

item_title: Anthropic's S-1/A states that strategic partners including Google and AMD agreed in November to buy $26.0 billion of its Class N common stock at the IPO price, in a private placement that closes immediately after the offering (Nov 10)
mechanism: Suppliers buying their largest customer's stock at the IPO price recycle part of their own sales into its capital, tying their returns to its demand for their chips and cloud.

scenarios.direction: The offering prices at or above the range and the suppliers' stakes mark up on listing, encouraging more equity-for-demand deals.
scenarios.why: The placement is priced at the IPO price, so a strong debut gives Google, Nvidia, AMD and the others an immediate paper gain on stock bought from a customer.
scenarios.precedent: Nvidia anchored CoreWeave's March 2025 IPO with a $250 million order, having invested in the company before it listed.

scenarios.direction: Weak demand forces a lower price, and the fixed $26.0 billion buys the strategic partners more shares at a lower valuation.
scenarios.why: The placement is set in dollars at whatever the IPO price turns out to be, so a cut range raises the buyers' share counts and dilutes other holders more.
scenarios.precedent: CoreWeave priced its March 2025 IPO at $40 a share, below its $47 to $55 range, and cut the number of shares offered.

scenarios.direction: Analysts and regulators question how much of the placement is new money and how much converts commitments already made.
scenarios.why: Google's purchase reduces its March 2026 note facility and AMD's satisfies an existing equity commitment, so part of the $26.0 billion replaces capital already promised.
scenarios.precedent: Nvidia's September 2025 letter of intent to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI drew wide commentary on circular AI financing.

item_title: CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3,661 million, against $1,365 million a year earlier, and a revenue backlog of about $132.5 billion at Sep 30 (Nov 10)
mechanism: Net interest of $846 million against $207 million of operating income means CoreWeave's growth is carried by debt whose cost runs ahead of its profits.

scenarios.direction: CoreWeave adds more contract- and chip-backed debt to fund the $37 billion to $39 billion of capital spending it guides for 2026.
scenarios.why: Spending at that pace runs far above revenue of about $3.7 billion a quarter, and the FT headline on a chip-backed debt deal points the same way.
scenarios.precedent: CoreWeave raised $7.5 billion of debt financing led by Blackstone and Magnetar in May 2024.

scenarios.direction: Customer prepayments fund a larger share of the build, shifting part of the financing risk onto customers.
scenarios.why: Its chief executive said about $9 billion of prepayments and deposits is expected in the next three months, cash that does not add to interest expense.

scenarios.direction: A weaker AI equity tape raises CoreWeave's borrowing costs and widens its losses.
scenarios.why: Nvidia fell about 9.5% in two days; with interest already above operating income, any rise in borrowing costs flows straight to the net loss.
